This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. praying to enlarge the petitioner on bail in Crime No.90/2023 registered at Mangalore Women Police Station, for the offence punishable under Sections 417, 376, 313 of IPC.

2. On completion of the investigation, the police have filed the charge sheet against the petitioner and another for the NC: 2024:KHC:2010 offence punishable under Sections 417, 376(2)(n), 313 and 109 of IPC.

3. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner, learned HCGP for the State, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/defacto complainant and perused the material on record.
4.
The case of the prosecution is that the complainant/victim is running a hookah shop in Saibeen complex situated in Lalbhag since three years.
She got acquainted with the accused who was visiting her shop.
They became close to each other.

On the pretext of marriage, on 15.05.2021 at about 12.30 p.m., the accused committed forcible sexual intercourse with the victim in the house of her grandmother and once again committed sexual intercourse with her in one S.S.Palace Apartment.
He continued to commit sexual intercourse with her on several occasions with a false promise of marriage.

In the year 2022, when she became pregnant, the accused gave her some tablets for terminating the pregnancy and even when she refused to take the tablets, his brother i.e., accused Mr. Jabir vs The State on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134331415/

5. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that even accepting the case of the prosecution as true, it is a clear case of consensual sex between the two from the year 2021 and no complaint was lodged.
He has contended that thinking she has become pregnant, victim has lodged a false complaint against the petitioner.

He has drawn the attention of the Court to the further statement of the victim recorded on 08.10.2023 and contended that while lodging the complaint,
she has mentioned that she was three months pregnant but later she was found to be not pregnant.
He has contended that in her further statement she has alleged that the petitioner wants to marry some other girl and therefore, she has lodged the complaint.
He has further contended that there is no material to show that the petitioner has given the tablets to the victim, consuming which her pregnancy was terminated.
Learned counsel has further contended that the petitioner is innocent and he is no way concerned to the alleged offence and he has been falsely implicated by the complainant with ulterior motives.
He submits that the petitioner is languishing in judicial custody since 06.10.2023.

Now the investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed and therefore, seeks to allow the petition.
7.
Learned HCGP has vehemently opposed the prayer contending that the victim has categorically stated about the heinous act committed by the accused.
She has also stated that her pregnancy was terminated by the accused by giving some tablets.

He contends that if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, he may try to influence the victim and also tamper with other prosecution witnesses and therefore, he has sought to dismiss the petition.
8.

Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/defacto complainant contended that the accused with a false promise of marriage has coerced the complainant to indulge in physical relationship with him and when she was conceived, with a criminal intention, administered tablets for NC:
2024:KHC:2010 terminating the pregnancy.

Drawing the attention of the Court to the statement of the Doctor - Hema Malya, he has contended that as per her statement, it is clear that the victim was pregnant and she was given tablets and subsequently, the scanning report also shows that she was pregnant of 07 to 08 weeks.

Therefore, he has contended that the petitioner has not only committed rape on the victim, in the guise of marriage but terminated the pregnancy by giving tablets to the victim which is a serious act, punishable with imprisonment for life.
He has contended that if the petitioner is enlarged on bail, he may try to influence and threaten the victim not to give evidence and therefore, seeks to dismiss the petition.

9. The complaint is lodged by the victim on 06.10.2023, on the basis of which case was registered against the petitioner and his brother - accused No.2 for the offence punishable under Sections 417,

sentences.text: A perusal of the complaint averments reveal that since three years, the petitioner and the victim were known to each other.
The first incidence of alleged rape is committed on 15.05.2021 at about 12.30 p.m. in the house of victim's grandmother.

It is alleged in the complaint that the victim conceived and when the NC: 2024:KHC:2010 petitioner gave some tablets, she refused to take it, but his brother i.e., accused No.2 called her and asked her to take the tablets so that he will talk to his brother and see that her marriage is performed with him.

It is alleged in the complaint that since four months, the petitioner was coming to the rented house of the victim and on 15.07.2023 at about 8 p.m. once again with a false promise to marry, he committed rape on her and thereafter, on several occasions repeated the said act and due to which she became pregnant.
10.
A perusal of victim's further statement reveals that after lodging of the complaint, when her medical examination was conducted, it was found that she was not pregnant.

In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she has stated that since three years, there was a love affair and they developed physical relationship, due to which she became five months pregnant.
11. The statement of the Doctor - Hema Malya recorded on 12.12.2023, reveal that the victim went to the clinic and took some tablets.
There is no material at this stage to show NC: 2024:KHC:2010 that it was the accused who purchased the tablets and got the pregnancy terminated.
12. The victim is a major aged about 28 years.
Even as per the complaint averments, the victim and the petitioner were known to each other for the last three years and on several occasions they indulged in sexual intercourse.
Even after termination of pregnancy, the victim continued physical relationship with the petitioner.

The allegations that the accused on a false pretext of marriage,
committed sexual intercourse with the victim or the consent was given under misconception of fact etc., is a matter which has to be established in a full - fledged trial.
The prosecution has to establish the ingredients of the offence alleged to have been committed by the accused.

13. Considering the above facts and circumstances and considering that the investigation is completed and charge sheet is already filed, the petitioner can be admitted to bail by imposing stringent conditions.

Accordingly, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:2010 ORDER Petition is allowed.

The petitioner/accused No.1 is directed to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.90/2023 of Mangalore Women Police Station subject to following conditions:
(i) Petitioner shall execute a personal bond in a sum of 1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with two sureties for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
(ii) Petitioner shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the IO/Court if there is any change in the address.
(iii) Petitioner shall not induce or intimidate the victim, either directly or indirectly.

(v) Petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission of the jurisdictional Court.
(vi) Petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court on every date of hearing without fail, unless exempted for genuine reasons.
If any of the above conditions are violated, the petitioner is not entitled for the benefit of this order.
The observation in the order shall not influence the trial of the case.
